knowledge_point.title: Finding a General Solution in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\sqrt{1-{\left(y-5\right)}^{2}}\,$ for $\,|\left(y-5\right)|<1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sqrt{1-{\left(y-5\right)}^{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-5\right)}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-5\right)}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-5\right)}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-5\right)}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y & =\int \text{d}x \\ \operatorname{arcsin}⁡\left(y-5\right) & =x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\operatorname{arcsin}⁡\left(y-5\right)=x+C.
$$

recipes: spurious factor two on right primitive

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3{\left(x+5\right)}^{2}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(y+2\right)}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3{\left(x+5\right)}^{2}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(y+2\right)} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡\left(y+2\right)\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3{\left(x+5\right)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡\left(y+2\right)\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 3{\left(x+5\right)}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\ \int \operatorname{cos}⁡\left(y+2\right)\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int 3{\left(x+5\right)}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\ \int \operatorname{cos}⁡\left(y+2\right)\,\text{d}y & =\int 3{\left(x+5\right)}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\left(y+2\right) & ={\left(x+5\right)}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(y+2\right)={\left(x+5\right)}^{3}+C.
$$

recipes: spurious factor two on right primitive

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=2{e}^{-\left(y-2\right)}(\left(x+3\right)-1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2{e}^{-\left(y-2\right)}(\left(x+3\right)-1) \\ {e}^{\left(y-2\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2(\left(x+3\right)-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {e}^{\left(y-2\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x & =\int 2(\left(x+3\right)-1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{\left(y-2\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int 2\left(x+3\right)\,\text{d}x-\int 2\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{\left(y-2\right)} & ={\left(x+3\right)}^{2}-2\left(x+3\right)+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
{e}^{\left(y-2\right)}={\left(x+3\right)}^{2}-2\left(x+3\right)+C.
$$

recipes: spurious factor two on right primitive
generation.domain: all real x,y; right side plus C>0
